title: Water climbing a thin tube
hook: Change tube radius and predict capillary-rise height.
misconception: capillary-rise height doubles when tube radius doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply h = 2γ cosθ/(ρgr) to compare capillary-rise height when tube radius changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With fixed surface tension density gravity and contact angle with a wetting liquid, h = 2γ cosθ/(ρgr). When tube radius doubles, capillary-rise height becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model h = 2γ cosθ/(ρgr); scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider fixed surface tension density gravity and contact angle with a wetting liquid, with a nonzero initial result. If tube radius triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on capillary-rise height?
recall.why: Apply h = 2γ cosθ/(ρgr) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
